destination.name: Anantara Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky
destination.note: The OSM point n251150450 in click-poi-info.json is reused as landmarkId. No installed model (including the Dam-square models de-bijenkorf, national-monument-on-the-dam, palace-on-the-dam) suppresses this pand; neighbours are not suppressed. BAG bouwjaar 1994 applies to the single large pand that contains the old hotel front and the modern wing.

sources.retrieved: 2026-10-10 (not read in full; used only for the link)

facts: Adolph Wilhelm Krasnapolsky bought the Nieuwe Poolse Koffiehuis on the Warmoesstraat in 1865; hotel rooms were added in 1879/1880 and a glass-and-iron Winter Garden with a domed roof was built in the back garden to a design by G.B. Salm.
After the Second World War the hotel grew south to the Pijlsteeg and north to the Sint Jansstraat; the address changed from Warmoesstraat 187-205 to Dam 9-15.
Operating as NH Collection Krasnapolsky after 2000 and as Anantara Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky since 2022.
The architect and date of the present Dam front are not stated in the sources read; the card does not claim one.

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012165293 LoD2.2, ground 1.164 m NAP, 166-vertex ring, about 130 m across. Dam front = gently curved chain of walls facing 307-316 degrees: 36, 27, 30, 361, 32, 33, 259, 39, 194 (modern stone wing, eave 16.3-20.5 m), 63, 68, 64, 72 (lower brick building, 20.3 m) and 73, 74 (old front, 25 m, 21.7 m). Walls above 20.2 m are the set-back glazed attic levels (up to 27.6 m) and are drawn as glass.
measuredBy.oldFront: From ref-dam-front-zoom2.jpg (about 50 px/m at the wall plane): bays at t = 1.9, 7.0, 12.0 (double windows 2.9 m wide, balconies on the first floor), entrance canopy with two lantern turrets at t 15-20, three narrow windows over the entrance, end window on wall 74, brick piers above a stone first floor, string courses at 10.9 and 17.8 m, cornice at 20.4 m. 2026-10-11: brick is limited to narrow piers (t = 4.4, 9.3, 14.3, 20.0) between the window groups; the rest is stone, as in the photo.
uncertain: Window counts on the modern wing and the lower brick building are read from oblique, tree-screened photographs (no frontal photo exists); integrator blind count pending.
Set-back glazed attic levels and rooftop volumes are the raw 3DBAG shell only.
Warmoesstraat, Sint Jansstraat and courtyard walls have no photographs (inferred, plain shell). Pijlsteeg side: blank brick wall evidenced, curved glass corner not modelled.
The roof sign on the old front is deliberately not modelled.
measuredBy.modernWing: Reworked 2026-10-11 from ref-dam-wide/ref-dam-ne/ref-dam-b-front: grey granite panels, dark steel-framed shopfront ground floor under a dark cornice band, large two-pane first-floor windows, tall paired narrow windows in black frames on a 2.5 m axis, three-storey projecting dark glass bays on every fourth axis. The set-back glazed attic levels come only from the 3DBAG shell.
measuredBy.lowerBuilding: Reworked 2026-10-11 from ref-dam-front-zoom: stone ground floor with large dark glass shopfront panels between piers, brick storeys with tall stone-framed paired windows, stone cornice.
measuredBy.partyWall: Faces SW (208 deg) on Pijlsteeg include a blank pale-brick wall about 14 m wide running the full height of the building (ref-sw-0.jpg, ref-sw-wide.jpg, panorama recording_2025-06-16_06-42-40_02265); spec.partyWallBearings [208] exempts it from the blank-wall check on that evidence. A curved dark-glass corner bay and granite columns next to it (ref-sw-wide2.jpg) are not modelled.
